Senses.PreferredTarget: to lift or hold up a physical object
Senses.Explanation: To lift, pick up, or hold aloft a physical object. The expression occurs 1,685 times in 307 allowlisted texts, with this concrete action repeatedly made into a visible move in public encounters. Shengguang holds up a whisk and asks what it is called. An unnamed newcomer lifts a sitting cloth and makes a circle. Nanquan Puyuan lifts the disputed cat and asks the assembly to speak. Deng Yinfeng lifts his rosary when asked his age, and an unnamed Chan visitor lifts a tea bowl when asked about ‘the other side.’ These constructions move an object bodily into view; they are distinct from instructions to take up and sustain a verbal question before attention.
Senses.Note: Concrete-object sense. Whisks, sitting cloths, an animal, rosary beads, and a tea bowl undergo bodily lifting or holding. Their different public uses do not create further senses, and no fixed symbolic force is assigned to the action.

Senses.PreferredTarget: to take up a saying or question for sustained attention
AlternateTargets: to bring a question to the fore
to hold up a saying for inquiry
SearchAliases: bring forward a topic of inquiry
Senses.Explanation: To take up a saying or question and keep it actively before attention. Zhongfeng Mingben repeatedly directs an assembly to do this with verbal objects: a saying without the flavor of meaning, one's assigned saying of inquiry, and the complete question ‘The myriad things return to one; where does the one return?’ His surrounding predicates require beginning with it, not moving from it, continuing forward with it, and sustaining questioning while walking or sitting. This is not bodily lifting of an object; it is the continued taking-up of a verbal subject.
Senses.Note: Discursive-attention sense. The three stored witnesses come from distinct instructions within Zhongfeng Mingben's record and use different verbal objects. They establish a different action from physical lifting, while variation among saying, assigned subject, and full question does not create further senses.
